chapter_note: Core substrate survives mainly as a cosmological/hierarchical depiction of the First Man’s commissioning, steadfastness in the worlds of darkness, and the purifying/separating work against the Enemy. A later sermonic/pastoral layer intensifies in the second half (esp. ¶6, ¶9), turning the cosmology into direct exhortation and introducing church categories (notably “catechumen”) as an interpretive graft. No explicit NT citation formula appears; the Christian-sounding titles (“only begotten”, “righteous”) function here as internal honorifics rather than Gospel overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.285⟩[ ... ] and the [righte]o[usness ... ] is more than [the ... ] the voice through them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly uncertain due to heavy lacunae and low lexical signals; no overt frame/pastoral markers remain, and the fragment reads like part of an impersonal teaching sequence rather than dialogue frame.
Dialogue attribution with “The a[postle] speaks [to] them …” functions as compilation frame (Layer 2); no recoverable substrate teaching is preserved in the surviving words.

paragraphs.core_text: This one, whom they called “approved” [ ... ... ] they approved him in the midst of the ae[ons of] light. These numerous multitudes set him a[part], and he came forth against the Enemy. They gave this name [ ... ... ] this matter [ ... ... ] who are numerous, that are in the aeons of light and who [are without] measure or number.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, cosmological commissioning scene: aeons of light, innumerable multitudes, being “set apart” and sent against the Enemy—cosmos→cosmos description without institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: This one, [whom they called] “righteous”, because he is the first righteous one who had no sin amongst all of the aeons that belong to the light and the thought [ ... ] they knew him, so that [ ... ] his Father, who had sent him with five sons [ ... ] perdition.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ecclesial/institutional identification: “becau]se he is the first catechumen [wh]o obe[y]ed” — a church category (‘catechumen’) applied to a cosmic being (cosmos→community mapping), likely a later sermonic/pastoral graft.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core logic is cosmic (primordial righteousness across the aeons; Father sending with five sons against perdition), but the ‘first catechumen’ phrase crosses into institutional present and reads like an editorial application inserted mid-sentence.

paragraphs.core_text: This one also [whom they called] “only begotten”, because he was established [ ... ] pour [ ... ] Enemy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Title-explication remains internal to the mythic commissioning; despite Christian resonance, there is no NT citation vector and the function is cosmological (a named role/epithet within the system).

Strong application voice (“I tell you, my brothers and my limbs”), moral modeling, and explicit community categories (catechumens/rebels). This is sermonic exhortation using the myth as precedent—editorial/pastoral layer, especially consistent with chapter’s fatigue drift.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, just as the only begotten ones from your [only] begotten race and you [ ... ] according to flesh [ ... ... o]nly begot-ten also from gold and silver and all the [ ... ] of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential/cosmological comparison (race/flesh alongside gold/silver/universe) with no direct exhortation; reads as internal teaching about ‘only-begotten’ status across registers.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.286⟩Just as your father, [the F]irst Man, himself stood firm in the [midst] of all the worlds of darkness. He did not love [the] worlds of darkness, nor did he lust for them! Rather, h[is] thought and love for the household of his people is in h[i]m. Anything else that the Enemy [ ... ] with his violent de[e]ds. Behold, (the First Man) toils and struggles; so that (the Enemy) would be separat[e from] them and be cast out from them. And he purifies them and ma[ke]s them f[r]ee, and makes them as they were from the beginning.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-process description (steadfastness in darkness; separation and purification; restoration ‘as from the beginning’). The possessive ‘your father’ sounds sermonic, but the substance remains cosmos→cosmos mechanics rather than institutional application.
Direct second-person exhortation (“You too… stand firm in this body… and all its lusts”) applies the myth to audience ascetic practice—application layer rather than substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] may they discover the remembrance of the household of his peo[ple], as he remains in this [place ni]ght and day.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary continuation of the ‘household of his people’ motif; likely still within the First Man mythic situation (‘remains… night and day’). The optative ‘may they’ could be rhetorical, but no clear institutional marker survives.
Formulaic closing: disciples rejoice, give glory, praise, obeisance—hagiographic frame wrapping the teaching.
